title: Structure grid: beginning, shift, ending
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Year 9 mastery and readiness for the International GCSE
source: Written for english/y9 lesson 77 (Structure grid: beginning, shift, ending (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 77: Unseen reading 3: structure: how a text develops. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

passage.title: Teacher-written extract for TGA
paras: The station was empty except for the pigeons and the clock. Platforms stretched away under yellow lights; a newspaper turned its pages in the draught. On the last bench sat a boy with a violin case on his knees, counting the minutes. When the train came, he did not get on. He watched its red lights shrink into the dark, then opened the case, took out a folded letter, and read it for the hundredth time. The station was empty again, except for the pigeons, the clock, and the boy.

head: Part
Focus
Effect
rows: wide view of the empty station
zooms in on the boy and the case
he does not get on: an unexpected action
returns to the empty station, now with the boy
cyclical; we see the scene differently

model.title: How does the writer structure the text to interest the reader?

parts.text: Point: the writer moves from wide to close
Evidence: from 'the station was empty' to 'a boy with a violin case'
Analysis: our curiosity grows as the focus narrows
Audience impact: we want to know why he stays
Link: the cyclical ending deepens the mystery

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The writer moves from a wide view of the empty station to a close focus on 'a boy with a violin case', so our curiosity grows as the frame narrows; the cyclical ending then returns us to the station, now changed by his mystery.

keywords.def: how a text is organised and develops
a change in focus, time, place or mood
moving from a wide view to a close detail

questions.q: Where is the first shift in focus?
questions.a: 'On the last bench sat a boy...'

questions.q: Core: complete a structure grid for a second unseen extract, then write a structure paragraph
Extend: explain why the writer withholds the letter's contents
questions.a: To create mystery and invite the reader to infer

questions.q: Stretch: rewrite the opening sentence to start with the boy and explain what is lost
Why does the ending repeat the opening with 'and the boy' added?
options: to show the same place now holds his story
because the writer ran out of ideas
questions.a: B) to show the same place now holds his story. The echo makes us look at the station again, now aware of the boy's mystery.
